title: Statistics-controlled topological phases in a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger ladder
authors: Rajashri Parida, Biswajit Paul, Smitha Vishveshwara, Diptiman Sen, Tapan Mishra
abstract: In strictly one-dimensional lattices, free fermions and hard-core bosons exhibit equivalent physical properties in many-particle systems. However, this statistical equivalence generally breaks down upon moving to higher dimensions. Our work investigates the significant effects of this difference on the topological phase transition in a minimal system lying away from one dimension: the two-leg Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) ladder. Starting in the limit of two decoupled SSH chains having opposite hopping dimerization patterns (staggered dimerization), we demonstrate that introducing inter-leg coupling drives a transition from a topological to a trivial phase for both spinless fermions and hard-core bosons. However, the topological to trivial phase transition boundary is strongly sensitive to the underlying particle statistics. We find that this intriguing effect favors a trivial phase sandwiched between the two topological phases with opposite characters for the case of hard-core bosons, resulting in a reentrant topological phase transition. In contrast, this reentrant phenomenon is absent for spinless fermions, with the topological phases being separated by a gapless line instead of an intervening trivial phase. This study demonstrates the interplay between particle statistics and topological features, revealing fundamentally different properties in an experimentally accessible set-up.
summary: This paper explores how particle statistics dictate the nature of topological phase transitions in a two-leg SSH ladder. By comparing spinless fermions and hard-core bosons, the authors find that bosons exhibit a reentrant topological transition separated by a trivial phase, whereas fermions are separated by a gapless line. This highlights the profound influence of statistics on emergent quantum phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates how the difference in particle statistics (spinless fermions versus hard-core bosons) affects the topological phase transition when moving from one dimension to a two-leg ladder structure.
main_result: Hard-core bosons exhibit a reentrant topological phase transition (Topological $	o$ Trivial $	o$ Topological), while spinless fermions transition between topological phases separated by a gapless critical line.
method: The research employs numerical simulations like DMRG and analytical techniques, including calculating topological invariants ($\gamma$) and using Thouless Charge Pumping (TCP) to probe the bulk topology.
model_or_system: The system is a two-leg Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) ladder, modeled using Hamiltonians for spinless fermions and hard-core bosons, incorporating hopping dimerization ($t_1, t_2$) and inter-leg coupling ($t_p$).
key_observables: Topological phase transitions, energy gap closures, quantized pumped charge ($|Q|$), and topological invariant ($\gamma$).
important_parameters: Hopping dimerization strength ($t_1$ vs. $t_2$), inter-leg coupling strength ($t_p$), and particle statistics (fermions vs. bosons).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing results in the 2-leg ladder geometry and utilizes approximations like the Hartree-Fock method for certain limits.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram in the $t_2 - t_p$ plane, comparing the topological regions for fermions and bosons, and showing the Rung Insulator phase for bosons.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the equivalence in 1D, then analyzes the 2-leg ladder, contrasting the gapless transition for fermions with the reentrant transition mediated by a trivial phase for bosons, using pumping measurements to confirm the statistical difference.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the fundamental role of particle statistics in determining macroscopic quantum properties like topological order, which is a key area of interest in strongly correlated quantum matter.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic of the two-leg SSH ladder. (b) Topo- logical bond order phase with edge modes localized on the upper leg (BO1). (c) Topological bond order phase with edge modes localized on the lower leg (BO−1). (d) Schematic of the rung insulator phase. The edge states reside on the upper (lower) leg in the BO1 (BO−1) phase. For both fermions and bosons, the rung insulator is characterized in terms of a sin- gle particle being dimerized on a single rung, and it can not move through the entire ladder except the rung in which it is trapped.

FIG. 2. The phase diagram in the t2 −tp plane for spinless fermions and hard-core bosons in (a) and (b) respectively. The red regions denote the topological bond-ordered phases (BO1 and BO−1), whereas the blue region indicates the triv- ial rung insulator phases (R-BI and RMI). The phase bound- aries marked by the blue squares demarcate the topological- to-trivial phase transitions in both the panels. The black dashed line in (a) is the gapless boundary between the two distinct topological phases which is absent in (b).

FIG. 3. Winding number γ/π (blue dashed) and bulk gap G (gray solid) at half-filling are plotted in (a), (b), and (d). The gap is finite for all the values of tp except at the transition point (tp ∼0.83). (b) The change in winding number from one to zero to one as a function of t2 indicates a reentrant topological phase transi- tion for hard-core bosons for fixed tp = 0.8.
